A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 15-page OmniBal paper, including Appendices A-K. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish matching scientific content, figures, tables, and equations.

before.justification: v4 reports original training-efficiency and benchmark results in Table 2, component ablations in Tables 3-7, and further experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including training costs, benchmark scores, ablations, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains identical iterative sampling and filtering, balanced model partitioning, and adaptive re-computation procedures, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is identical, including InternVL-1.2M, LLaVA-665K, LCS-558K, the five benchmark families in Table 2, and appendix pretraining and image-resolution scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same DeepSpeed and Megatron-DeepSpeed configurations, length-group and device-group methods, and parameter-, layer-, and profile-based partition baselines.

E3.justification: Experimental settings and metrics in Section 5 and the appendices are identical, including sample counts, model configurations, preprocessing, hardware configurations, and GPU-day reporting.

E4.justification: Tables 3-7 retain the same component and threshold ablations. Figure 4 and Appendix G retain identical ISF convergence analyses across datasets, patch settings, and resolutions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the variability summaries in Table 1 and Figure 2. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains 61.8 and 21.3 GPU days for unbalanced and balanced 6+20B Megatron training, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are identical, including the padding and distribution ratios, partition-selection objective, partition-ranking formulas, and stated ISF complexity.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying VLM computation imbalance and addressing it through coordinated data, model, and memory balancing to accelerate training while maintaining performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications are identical, including the interdependence of the three balancing components and Appendix H's explanation of smaller acceleration for LLaVA's relatively small vision encoder.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 and the appendices disclose identical thresholds, profiling procedures, partition and re-computation configurations, and hardware details. The code-release statement and repository address are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, references, and novelty positioning are identical; no prior work is added, removed, or substantively recharacterized.

P1.justification: Only the first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes, from v4 dated 29 May 2025 to v5 dated 13 October 2025. The paper's prose, headings, terminology, and organization are identical.

P2.justification: All four figures and sixteen tables retain identical displays, captions, and placement. Rendered pages 2-15 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the version/date stamp text, with no layout change.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and presentation are unchanged throughout the main paper and appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
